raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo`, GLM-5.x (DSA with shared top-k layers, `index_topk_freq > 1`) loses about a third of its GSM8K accuracy: 0.93 with DBO off, 0.61 with DBO on. The layers that reuse an earlier layer's sparse-attention top-k (57 of GLM-5.3's 78 layers) read it from buffers that have no microbatch dimension. DBO runs microbatch 1's index-producing layer between microbatch 0's producer and its consumers, so microbatch 0's consumers attend over microbatch 1's token selection. This PR gives every DBO microbatch after the first its own copy of that state. With it, DBO-on accuracy matches DBO off.

Companion to #60732 (DSA indexer crash under DBO, which hid this bug). The two fixes are independent; DBO with DeepEP high-throughput needs both. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `dbo topk`, `index_topk_freq dbo`, `shared indexer microbatch`, `GLM-5 dbo accuracy`: 0 results). Related open PR: #56476 fixes the same class of bug for DeepSeek-V4.1 (its top-k and candidate buffers, via a new `dbo_select_buffer` helper). It does not cover the DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.x IndexCache path changed here; if it lands first, this PR can switch to its helper.

## Claims

- Fixes GLM-5.x accuracy under DBO on Model Runner V1 and V2: GSM8K 0.61 → 0.92 (DBO off: 0.92–0.93). Also with DBO microbatches replayed from FULL decode CUDA graphs (DeepEP low-latency): 0.44 → 0.85 (DBO off: 0.84–0.86).
- No change without DBO, and none for DSA models without shared top-k layers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1: every layer computes its own top-k, so no microbatch state is allocated). Measured: both score the same with DBO on as off, with and without this change, and report identical KV cache memory with and without it.
- Memory under DBO, per GPU and per extra microbatch: `(max_num_batched_tokens + G * (max_decode_rows + 1)) * index_topk * 4` bytes, where `G` is the number of index groups with followers (19 for GLM-5.3). GLM-5.3 at `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=1024`: 216 MiB, measured as 0.22 GiB less KV cache memory.
- No host syncs, no extra kernels. The per-microbatch lookup is one dict read per access, the same one DBO already uses everywhere (`dbo_current_ubatch_id()`).
- HiSparse with DBO and shared top-k layers now raises at startup (it previously ran with the same corruption); supporting it needs per-microbatch HiSparse staging, out of scope here.

## Validation

**Unit test (new)**, `test_sparse_mla_index_group_keeps_topk_per_dbo_ubatch` in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: one leader group without followers and one with a follower, built with `num_ubatches=2`. It checks that the leader-only group allocates nothing, that leader and follower impls resolve to the same per-microbatch buffer, and that after both microbatches' leaders write (in DBO order: leader 0, leader 1, then followers) each follower's logical and converted physical top-k equal its own leader's bit for bit. Runs in the existing "V1 Attention" CI shards.

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| this branch | passed |
| base (without fix) | fails (the builder has no `num_ubatches`) |
| mutation: index group always returns microbatch 0's state | fails |
| mutation: impl not wired to the per-microbatch logical buffers | fails |

The two mutations each break one half of the fix and confirm the assertions catch it. Existing tests on this branch (H200): `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 293 passed (1,188 skipped by hardware), `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` + `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` 40 passed. `tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, DP2, DBO): 2 passed (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`). pre-commit's ruff check and format pass; mypy on the four changed source files reports no new errors (two fewer than base).

All tests and GPU runs in this description used main @ 4a705c7b. This branch is rebased onto main @ 240785b8, where the five files it changes differ only in HiSparse code it does not touch (`HiSparseMLAIndexGroup` routing, #60682; HiSparse tests, #60429 and #60682), and `ubatching.py` / `ubatch_utils.py` are unchanged. Re-run on the rebased commit (H200): the new test passes (and still fails on main without the fix), `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` 293 passed (1,188 skipped), `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py` and `test_gpu_ubatch_slicing.py` 40 passed, and `pytest -v -s tests/v1/distributed/test_dbo.py` 2 passed (`deepep_low_latency`, `deepep_high_throughput`). The GSM8K and long-prompt runs were not repeated on the new base.

**Model evaluation, GLM-5.3 FP8** (1 x 8 H200, DP4 x TP2, EP8, DeepEP high-throughput unless noted, `cudagraph_mode NONE`, fp8 KV, prefix caching, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`; `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 questions, `num_concurrent=256`; standard error ±0.007 at 0.92, ±0.013 at 0.61). Every DBO-on run microbatched 100+ steps per worker.

| vLLM | Runner | DBO | GSM8K flexible / strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| main + #60732 | V2 | off | 0.927 / 0.928 |
| main + #60732 | V1 | off | 0.924 / 0.924 |
| main + #60732 | V1 | on | 0.613 / 0.607 |
| main + #60732 | V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`) | on | 0.614 / 0.610 |
| main + #60732 + this PR | V1 | on | 0.922 / 0.923 |
| main + #60732 + this PR (repeat) | V1 | on | 0.923 / 0.921 |
| main + #60732 + this PR | V2 | on | 0.919 / 0.919 |
| main + this PR only, `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | V1 | on | 0.923 / 0.923 |

Note that `--enable-dbo` alone falls back to Model Runner V1; the V2 rows set `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` (logs confirm "Using V2 Model Runner" and "Dual batch overlap is enabled").

**CUDA graphs** (DBO microbatches replayed from FULL decode graphs). This needs DeepEP low-latency (high-throughput cannot be captured) and pure decode steps on every DP rank, which `lm_eval`'s streaming load never produces at low-latency's 256-token step budget (0 microbatched steps in a full GSM8K run). Workload instead: the first 1,024 GSM8K test questions zero-shot, sent at once (256 per DP rank), 192 forced greedy tokens each, scored for the final answer. Same GLM-5.3 setup with `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, `cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, Model Runner V1 in all runs. These runs also carry a one-line fix for a separate bug: the batched Triton FP8 MoE that low-latency mode uses (with DeepGEMM off) does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` to the 128-wide FP8 block (`fused_batched_moe.py:452`, unlike `fused_moe.py:844`), which gives GSM8K 0.02 even with DBO off; with the clamp, 0.93. That fix is its own PR (#60733).

With `--max-num-batched-tokens 512` (`NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH=4096`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`, so the prompts prefill in about 50 steps and most answer tokens are decoded in microbatched steps), each DBO-on worker replayed 180+ microbatched decode graphs and ran 50+ eager microbatched prefill steps:

| Run (1,024 questions, low-latency, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`) | Accuracy | vs DBO off #1: lost / gained (McNemar z) |
|---|---|---|
| DBO off #1 | 0.843 | |
| DBO off #2 | 0.857 | 11 / 26 (-2.5) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0.440 | 442 / 30 (19.0) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 0.845 | 40 / 42 (-0.2) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR (repeat) | 0.850 | 31 / 38 (-0.8) |

At the default 256-token budget (fewer microbatched steps) the picture is the same: DBO off 0.849 / 0.848, without this PR 0.775 (z 6.4 vs off), with it 0.838 (z 1.4). Exact token sequences are not a usable signal in this mode: two DBO-off runs already differ at the first token for 100 of 1,024 prompts.

**Negative control, GLM-5.1 FP8** (DSA, `index_topk_freq=1`: no shared top-k layers), same setup (main + #60732): DBO off 0.946 / 0.948; DBO on without this PR 0.952 / 0.950; DBO on with this PR 0.947 / 0.950 (100+ microbatched steps per worker in both DBO runs). With and without this PR the DBO-on runs report the same model memory (100.48 GiB) and KV cache memory (15.16 GiB): nothing is allocated when every layer computes its own top-k. DSA plus DBO is fine when no layer reuses another's top-k.

**Second negative control, DeepSeek-V3.2** (61 layers, every one computes its own top-k), same setup. Note: in this configuration vLLM main crashes with an illegal memory access in the first microbatched profiling step for DeepSeek-V3.2 with DBO on, with or without either fix (also without #60732, where it shows up as a DeepEP timeout instead). It disappears with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, so it is a separate stream race, not investigated here. The DBO-on runs below therefore use `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, which keeps DBO's microbatch order: GLM-5.3 without this PR still shows this bug under it (0.607 / 0.596, vs 0.613 / 0.607 without blocking).

| DeepSeek-V3.2 | GSM8K flexible / strict | Long prompts vs DBO off: differ at token 0, median \|Δ logprob\| | KV cache memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second DBO-off run = noise floor) | 0.952 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0001 | 24.46 GiB |
| DBO on, without this PR | 0.954 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |
| DBO on, with this PR | 0.952 / 0.951 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |

**Isolating the cause** (GLM-5.3, main + #60732, DBO on):

| Experiment | GSM8K flexible | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| DBO only on decode steps | 0.601 | decode steps alone reproduce the full drop |
| DBO only on prefill steps (3 microbatched steps) | 0.901 | few prefill splits, small drop |
| prefix caching off | 0.619 | not prefix caching |
| `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | 0.610 | not the DeepGEMM SM partition |
| prototype: per-microbatch converted (physical) top-k only, logical buffer still shared | 0.920 | short steps only read the converted copy |

**Long prompts, greedy** (GLM-5.3, same setup, Model Runner V1): 128 GSM8K-train prompts of 4.5k–7.7k tokens sent at once (prefill steps microbatch as 2 x 4096), 32 greedy tokens each with logprobs, compared against a DBO-off run. A second DBO-off run gives the noise floor (batching is not invariant, so long greedy continuations drift even without DBO).

| Run vs. DBO off | Identical 32-token outputs | Mean first differing token | Differ at token 0 | Median \|Δ logprob\| of token 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second run) | 35 / 128 | 18.2 | 0 | 0.0001 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0 / 128 | 3.0 | 7 | 0.0135 |
| DBO on, prototype with only the converted (physical) top-k per microbatch | 2 / 128 | 3.4 | 10 | 0.0081 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 24 / 128 | 17.1 | 0 | 0.0001 |

A step with more tokens than the conversion workspace (`max_decode_rows + 1`, 1,025 here) skips the cached conversion, and every follower converts from the logical buffer again. That is why the prototype fixes GSM8K but not long prefills, and why this PR keeps both the logical buffer and the converted state per microbatch.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dbo_ubatch

# GSM8K (add VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 for Model Runner V2)
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main @ 240785b8). GLM-5.x configs set `index_topk_freq=4`, `index_skip_topk_offset=3`: only 21 of 78 layers run the sparse indexer ("leaders": 0, 1, 2, 6, 10, …, 74); each of the other 57 reuses the top-k of the leader before it. That hand-off goes through state with no microbatch dimension:
- the model-wide logical buffer `DeepseekV32Model.topk_indices_buffer`, which the leader writes (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer`) and every follower's sparse MLA impl reads;
- per index group, `SparseMLAIndexGroup.physical_topk_indices` / `valid_topk_counts` (logical → physical conversion, done once by the leader and reused by its followers) and the `logical_topk_ready` / `physical_topk_ready` events.

DBO yields inside MoE dispatch/combine, so between microbatch 0's leader L and its follower L+1, microbatch 1 runs its own layer L and overwrites all of the above. Every follower of microbatch 0 except layer 3 (layers 0–2 are dense, so there is no yield between leader 2 and follower 3) then attends over microbatch 1's selected tokens, with block-table conversion done for microbatch 1's requests. Microbatch 1's followers read their own data and are unaffected. Leaders without followers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1, layers 0 and 1 here) are unaffected because they write and read within one layer.

**How it was found:** while validating #60732, GSM8K with DBO on came out at ~0.6 against 0.93 off, with or without that fix and with SM partitioning disabled. The table above narrowed it to decode-step microbatching independent of prefix caching and SM count; GLM-5.1 (same architecture, no shared top-k) was unaffected, which pointed at the shared top-k hand-off. A prototype that gave each microbatch its own converted top-k restored 0.920; the long-prompt test below shows it is not enough on its own.

**Fix:**
- `SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder` takes `num_ubatches`. When a group gets its first follower, it allocates one `UbatchTopkState` (physical indices, valid counts, two events) per extra microbatch for that group, and, once per builder, one logical buffer per extra microbatch. Groups without followers allocate nothing.
- `SparseMLAIndexGroup._topk_state()` and `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer.topk_indices_buffer` return microbatch 0's existing state, or the extra microbatch's copy when `dbo_current_ubatch_id() > 0`.
- The leader's writers (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer` in `DeepseekV32Attention`) now take the buffer from `self.impl.topk_indices_buffer`, so writer and readers resolve the same per-microbatch buffer.
- `DeepseekV32Model` passes `num_ubatches=get_num_ubatches(parallel_config)`.

The extra buffers are allocated at model construction, before the KV-cache profile, so they come out of KV cache memory. In FULL-graph DBO capture, each microbatch thread resolves its own buffers at capture time.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

1. Add a microbatch dimension to `topk_indices_buffer` itself: touches the MTP proposer's buffer sharing and every reader; the per-impl property was already the single resolution point.
2. Make followers recompute top-k under DBO: correct but runs the indexer on all 78 layers, which is what `index_topk_freq` exists to avoid.
3. Disable DBO for models with shared top-k layers: loses the overlap for exactly the models (GLM-5.x) that use DBO in production.
4. Allocate per-microbatch state in every index group: wastes memory for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1, which have no followers.
</details>

**MTP:** the draft's indexers are re-pointed to the target buffer through the module setter, which clears any microbatch buffers. The MTP layer is a leader-only group and the draft runs outside the microbatch threads, so it is unchanged.

**Not covered:** the ROCm DSA model (`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd`) and the non-CUDA fallback in `deepseek_v2.py`/`glm4_moe_lite.py` still build their groups with one microbatch; they keep the old behavior if they run DBO with shared top-k layers. HiSparse raises instead (see Claims).

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

---

These runs also carry a one-line fix for a separate bug: the batched Triton FP8 MoE that low-latency mode uses (with DeepGEMM off) does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` to the 128-wide FP8 block (`fused_batched_moe.py:452`, unlike `fused_moe.py:844`), which gives GSM8K 0.02 even with DBO off; with the clamp, 0.93. That fix is its own PR (#60733).

With `--max-num-batched-tokens 512` (`NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH=4096`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`, so the prompts prefill in about 50 steps and most answer tokens are decoded in microbatched steps), each DBO-on worker replayed 180+ microbatched decode graphs and ran 50+ eager microbatched prefill steps:

| Run (1,024 questions, low-latency, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`) | Accuracy | vs DBO off #1: lost / gained (McNemar z) |
|---|---|---|
| DBO off #1 | 0.843 | |
| DBO off #2 | 0.857 | 11 / 26 (-2.5) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0.440 | 442 / 30 (19.0) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 0.845 | 40 / 42 (-0.2) |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR (repeat) | 0.850 | 31 / 38 (-0.8) |

At the default 256-token budget (fewer microbatched steps) the picture is the same: DBO off 0.849 / 0.848, without this PR 0.775 (z 6.4 vs off), with it 0.838 (z 1.4). Exact token sequences are not a usable signal in this mode: two DBO-off runs already differ at the first token for 100 of 1,024 prompts.

**Negative control, GLM-5.1 FP8** (DSA, `index_topk_freq=1`: no shared top-k layers), same setup (main + #60732): DBO off 0.946 / 0.948; DBO on without this PR 0.952 / 0.950; DBO on with this PR 0.947 / 0.950 (100+ microbatched steps per worker in both DBO runs). With and without this PR the DBO-on runs report the same model memory (100.48 GiB) and KV cache memory (15.16 GiB): nothing is allocated when every layer computes its own top-k. DSA plus DBO is fine when no layer reuses another's top-k.

**Second negative control, DeepSeek-V3.2** (61 layers, every one computes its own top-k), same setup. Note: in this configuration vLLM main crashes with an illegal memory access in the first microbatched profiling step for DeepSeek-V3.2 with DBO on, with or without either fix (also without #60732, where it shows up as a DeepEP timeout instead). It disappears with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, so it is a separate stream race, not investigated here. The DBO-on runs below therefore use `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, which keeps DBO's microbatch order: GLM-5.3 without this PR still shows this bug under it (0.607 / 0.596, vs 0.613 / 0.607 without blocking).

| DeepSeek-V3.2 | GSM8K flexible / strict | Long prompts vs DBO off: differ at token 0, median \|Δ logprob\| | KV cache memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second DBO-off run = noise floor) | 0.952 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0001 | 24.46 GiB |
| DBO on, without this PR | 0.954 / 0.952 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |
| DBO on, with this PR | 0.952 / 0.951 | 0, 0.0000 | 23.22 GiB |

**Isolating the cause** (GLM-5.3, main + #60732, DBO on):

| Experiment | GSM8K flexible | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| DBO only on decode steps | 0.601 | decode steps alone reproduce the full drop |
| DBO only on prefill steps (3 microbatched steps) | 0.901 | few prefill splits, small drop |
| prefix caching off | 0.619 | not prefix caching |
| `VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0` | 0.610 | not the DeepGEMM SM partition |
| prototype: per-microbatch converted (physical) top-k only, logical buffer still shared | 0.920 | short steps only read the converted copy |

**Long prompts, greedy** (GLM-5.3, same setup, Model Runner V1): 128 GSM8K-train prompts of 4.5k–7.7k tokens sent at once (prefill steps microbatch as 2 x 4096), 32 greedy tokens each with logprobs, compared against a DBO-off run. A second DBO-off run gives the noise floor (batching is not invariant, so long greedy continuations drift even without DBO).

| Run vs. DBO off | Identical 32-token outputs | Mean first differing token | Differ at token 0 | Median \|Δ logprob\| of token 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DBO off (second run) | 35 / 128 | 18.2 | 0 | 0.0001 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 | 0 / 128 | 3.0 | 7 | 0.0135 |
| DBO on, prototype with only the converted (physical) top-k per microbatch | 2 / 128 | 3.4 | 10 | 0.0081 |
| DBO on, main + #60732 + this PR | 24 / 128 | 17.1 | 0 | 0.0001 |

A step with more tokens than the conversion workspace (`max_decode_rows + 1`, 1,025 here) skips the cached conversion, and every follower converts from the logical buffer again. That is why the prototype fixes GSM8K but not long prefills, and why this PR keeps both the logical buffer and the converted state per microbatch.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k dbo_ubatch

# GSM8K (add VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 for Model Runner V2)
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput --enable-dbo --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "NONE"}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause** (main @ 240785b8). GLM-5.x configs set `index_topk_freq=4`, `index_skip_topk_offset=3`: only 21 of 78 layers run the sparse indexer ("leaders": 0, 1, 2, 6, 10, …, 74); each of the other 57 reuses the top-k of the leader before it. That hand-off goes through state with no microbatch dimension:
- the model-wide logical buffer `DeepseekV32Model.topk_indices_buffer`, which the leader writes (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer`) and every follower's sparse MLA impl reads;
- per index group, `SparseMLAIndexGroup.physical_topk_indices` / `valid_topk_counts` (logical → physical conversion, done once by the leader and reused by its followers) and the `logical_topk_ready` / `physical_topk_ready` events.

DBO yields inside MoE dispatch/combine, so between microbatch 0's leader L and its follower L+1, microbatch 1 runs its own layer L and overwrites all of the above. Every follower of microbatch 0 except layer 3 (layers 0–2 are dense, so there is no yield between leader 2 and follower 3) then attends over microbatch 1's selected tokens, with block-table conversion done for microbatch 1's requests. Microbatch 1's followers read their own data and are unaffected. Leaders without followers (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.1, layers 0 and 1 here) are unaffected because they write and read within one layer.

**How it was found:** while validating #60732, GSM8K with DBO on came out at ~0.6 against 0.93 off, with or without that fix and with SM partitioning disabled. The table above narrowed it to decode-step microbatching independent of prefix caching and SM count; GLM-5.1 (same architecture, no shared top-k) was unaffected, which pointed at the shared top-k hand-off. A prototype that gave each microbatch its own converted top-k restored 0.920; the long-prompt test below shows it is not enough on its own.

**Fix:**
- `SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder` takes `num_ubatches`. When a group gets its first follower, it allocates one `UbatchTopkState` (physical indices, valid counts, two events) per extra microbatch for that group, and, once per builder, one logical buffer per extra microbatch. Groups without followers allocate nothing.
- `SparseMLAIndexGroup._topk_state()` and `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer.topk_indices_buffer` return microbatch 0's existing state, or the extra microbatch's copy when `dbo_current_ubatch_id() > 0`.
- The leader's writers (`fused_norm_rope`, `sparse_attn_indexer` in `DeepseekV32Attention`) now take the buffer from `self.impl.topk_indices_buffer`, so writer and readers resolve the same per-microbatch buffer.
- `DeepseekV32Model` passes `num_ubatches=get_num_ubatches(parallel_config)`.

The extra buffers are allocated at model construction, before the KV-cache profile, so they come out of KV cache memory. In FULL-graph DBO capture, each microbatch thread resolves its own buffers at capture time.

<details>
<summary>Alternatives considered</summary>

1. Add a microbatch dimension to `topk_indices_buffer` itself: touches the MTP proposer's buffer sharing and every reader; the per-impl property was already the single resolution point.
2. Make followers recompute top-k under DBO: correct but runs the indexer on all 78 layers, which is what `index_topk_freq` exists to avoid.
3. Disable DBO for models with shared top-k layers: loses the overlap for exactly the models (GLM-5.x) that use DBO in production.
4. Allocate per-microbatch state in every index group: wastes memory for DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1, which have no followers.
</details>

**MTP:** the draft's indexers are re-pointed to the target buffer through the module setter, which clears any microbatch buffers. The MTP layer is a leader-only group and the draft runs outside the microbatch threads, so it is unchanged.

**Not covered:** the ROCm DSA model (`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd`) and the non-CUDA fallback in `deepseek_v2.py`/`glm4_moe_lite.py` still build their groups with one microbatch; they keep the old behavior if they run DBO with shared top-k layers. HiSparse raises instead (see Claims).

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

+        num_extra = self.num_ubatches - 1
+        if not self.ubatch_logical_topk_indices:
+            self.ubatch_logical_topk_indices.extend(
+                torch.empty_like(self.logical_topk_indices) for _ in range(num_extra)
+            )
+        group.ubatch_states = tuple(
+            UbatchTopkState(
+                physical_topk_indices=torch.empty_like(group.physical_topk_indices),
+                valid_topk_counts=torch.empty_like(group.valid_topk_counts),
+                logical_topk_ready=_create_event(),
+                physical_topk_ready=_create_event(),
+            )
+            for _ in range(num_extra)
+        )
+
